facts.claim: A context window is all the text a model can reference when answering, like working or short-term memory
In a standard chat setup each turn sends the earlier conversation plus the new message back in as input
More context is not automatically better: as token count grows accuracy and recall can degrade, called context rot
When a chat nears the limit some apps summarize earlier messages to make room
A summary is shorter than the original, so some exact details can blur or be lost
Chroma tested many popular models: reliability dropped as input grew, even on simple tasks
Details that look similar to the right one but are wrong distract models more as input grows
Models often use information at the start or end of a long input best, and information in the middle less well, even long-context models
Results vary by model and task, and Chroma did not see the same U-shaped pattern, so placement is not a reliable rule
A short focused input did much better than a full input padded with irrelevant content; curating context matters
Google advises putting the question at the end of a long prompt; start and end are used most reliably

post.pinned_comment: The person in this story is fictional and the story is an illustration. The facts come from Anthropic and Google documentation, the Lost in the Middle research paper, and the Chroma context rot study as reported by independent write-ups. Results vary by model and app, and some chat apps handle long chats differently. The two tips at the end are practical suggestions, not guarantees.
